title: Invocation Snapshot Explorer - prototype notes
content:
Summary:

This doc collects UX notes and quick wireframe iterations for the Invocation Snapshot Explorer (ISE) — a compact inspector that surfaces per-invocation cost and latency decomposition at the granularity of individual model tokens / generation steps. Goal is to let engineers and product owners quickly answer: why did this request cost X and take Yms, and which parts of the prompt or model behavior contributed most?

High level goals:
- Fast triage: show a single-pane breakdown for one invocation with tappable detail expansion.
- Compare mode: side-by-side snapshots of two invocations (e.g., baseline vs. regression).
- Attribution: attribute token-cost and token-latency to prompt segments, system messages, and streaming output.
- Privacy-sensible: option to redact user content while preserving timing/cost signals.

Primary personas and scenarios:
- Eng on-call: investigating why a customer reported slow responses for a specific request id. Needs quick hotspot identification and link to trace.
- Performance PM: comparing model/quantization A vs B for a canonical prompt set. Wants per-step cost delta.
- Customer success / Solutions eng: explain cost drivers to a customer and recommend config changes.

Interaction primitives (core elements):
- Snapshot header: invocation id, model name + version, route, timestamp, total tokens, total cost estimate (USD), total latency (ms), status. Quick action buttons: open full trace, copy invocation JSON, redact content.
- Strand view (primary visualization): horizontal row per token showing a thin bar sized to that token's compute cost with color intensity encoding latency contribution. Bars are ordered left-to-right in generation order. Hover/tap opens token detail.
- Heat-strip overlay: aggregated per-100-token density visualization for long responses (zoomable).
- Segment anchors: ability to annotate ranges that map to prompt segments (system / user / instruction / tool output).
- Waterfall toggle: show the classic waterfall view for timing alignment (useful for SREs).
- Compare slider: when in compare mode, a central slider aligns two strand views by token index or by timestamp. Deltas are visualized as thin red/green ticks above tokens.

Wireframe iterations (notes):
Iteration A - single-column, dense strand- Pros: compact, scannable for small responses (<=200 tokens). - Cons: hard to compare across invocations.

Iteration B - split header + expandable token table- Introduces a token table beneath the strand with columns: idx, token_text (redacted by default), token_cost, token_latency, kv-cache-hit flag, sequence_source (prompt/system/tool). - Pros: more explicit numbers for billing and SLOs. - Cons: large vertical scroll for long generations.

Iteration C - compare-first layout (prototype we sketched last week)- Two aligned strands, diff ticks, per-column hover cross-highlight. - Pros: immediate visual delta for A/B testing. - Cons: UI complexity and cognitive load for first-time users.

Design decisions to lock before dev:
1) Cost attribution model: do we show raw GPU cost estimate, normalized per-1000-tokens cost, or Redwood billing estimate? Proposal: show Redwood billing estimate in main header and provide GPU-cost proxy in a tooltip.
2) Redaction default: user content redacted by default on shared links; internal view shows raw text. Add checkbox in header.
3) Sampling for long traces: cap default view at first 400 tokens and provide an on-demand scan & sample algorithm (head/tail/random sample) to avoid rendering lag.
4) Aggregation granularity: token-level always available via table, visualization supports bucket sizes [1,5,25,100]. Default bucket=1 for short responses, 25 for >200 tokens.

Data & instrumentation needs (engineering ask):
- Per-invocation: token sequence with per-token latency (time-to-first-byte and time-to-generation), compute_cycles_estimate, token_byte_length, kv_cache_hit boolean, model_kernel_tag (if available).
- Sampling triggers emitted by runtime when invocation length > 400 to enable head/tail sampling.
- Link from invocation to full trace id and to route-level cost metadata.

Open questions / risks:
- Cost noise: per-token cost estimates vary with batching and hardware; must show confidence/variance.
- Privacy: token text is sensitive; ensure short-lived redacted snapshots and an audit trail when unredacting.
- Performance: browser rendering of thousands of bars is expensive. Plan to use canvas renderer + virtualized token list.
- Naming: Invocation Snapshot Explorer vs. Token Strand Inspector vs. Invocation Timeline. Consensus leaning to "Invocation Snapshot" because it maps well to existing telemetry concepts.

Acceptance criteria for an initial release (MVP):
- Show header with total cost and latency for an invocation and at least 1 visualization mode (strand or bucketed heat-strip).
- Hover/tap token view shows token-index, source segment, token_latency_ms, token_cost_usd estimate, and KV cache flag.
- Deep link to full trace and copy-invocation button.
- Sampling behavior for invocations > 400 tokens configured with default head-only + tail sampling.

Edge cases & UX polish items:
- Empty responses or truncated responses: show friendly explanation and link to sampling trace.
- Very long tokens (in bytes): collapse display and show byte-length tooltip.
- Multi-model fanout (router routed to 2 models): show per-model strand stacked vertically with an option to merge into single virtualized timeline.

Backlog & next steps:
- RFC for data schema (ENG-CON-req) to include per-token fields above (owner: Arjun). Target: 2025-02-10.
- Prototype in Figma (Leah) with 3 states: single snapshot, compare two snapshots, and redacted-share modal. Target: 2025-01-22.
- Spike: canvas rendering perf test for 2k token bars (SRE/FE pairing). Diego to run. Target: 2025-01-20.
- Jira tickets to implement MVP: JIRA-CON-678 (frontend), JIRA-CON-679 (api/telemetry), JIRA-CON-680 (redaction/audit).

Notes from last pairing session (2025-01-15):
- PM asked to prioritize compare mode for model-release regressions.
- SRE emphasized need to link to sampled kernel logs to explain outlier latency spikes.
- Legal flagged sharing constraints for PII; add retention TTL on shared snapshot links.

Design alternatives we discussed and intentionally deprioritized:
- Showing per-layer GPU memory usage per token (nice-to-have, complex to collect).
- Animated streaming playback of token generation aligned to timestamps (cool for demos but heavy for debugging flows).

Quick mockup checklist for Figma handover:
- Components: strand-bar, heat-strip, token-detail-popover, compare-slider, header-actions, redaction-modal, sampled-view-switch.
- Tokens sample dataset: generate 6 canonical prompts across sizes [20, 80, 300, 900, 2100] with synthetic kernel_tags to test stacked model fanouts.
- Accessibility: ensure colorblind-safe palette and allow numeric overlays on bars.

Decision log (so far):
- Use Redwood billing estimate in header (decided 2025-01-10).
- Redaction default ON for shared links (decided 2025-01-15).

If you're reviewing: please comment inline on which visualization you find most actionable (strand vs. bucketed heat-strip), and whether we should expose a per-token cost confidence interval.

-- end --
